title: Rights, Respect & Fair Treatment at Work
summary: Learn how respect, fairness, workplace rights, responsibilities, and appropriate reporting channels contribute to a professional workplace.
objectives: Recognize the importance of fair and respectful treatment at work.
Identify concerning workplace behavior that may require support or reporting.
Explain why workplace rights and policies can vary by role, employer, location, and applicable law.

vocab.def: Applying workplace expectations and decisions in a respectful, appropriate, and non-arbitrary way.
Unfair treatment based on a characteristic protected by applicable law or policy.
Unwelcome behavior that may violate workplace policy or applicable law depending on the circumstances.
Adverse treatment connected to someone raising a protected or policy-covered concern, where applicable.

sections.heading: Respect is a workplace expectation
sections.body: Professional workplaces should support respectful communication, fair treatment, and clear standards. Workers should not be expected to tolerate mistreatment simply because it occurs at work.

sections.heading: Some concerns involve policy or legal protections
sections.body: Discrimination, harassment, retaliation, wage issues, safety concerns, and other workplace-rights questions may be governed by employer policy and applicable law. The exact rules can differ by location and situation.

sections.heading: Know where to ask for help
sections.body: A workplace may provide supervisors, human resources, compliance contacts, safety channels, union representatives, or other authorized resources for questions and concerns.

sections.heading: Do not make legal conclusions beyond your role
sections.body: Workers can recognize that something appears concerning and report it through the appropriate process without claiming to make the final legal or institutional determination themselves.

practice.prompt: A coworker describes treatment that seems unfair and asks you to decide whether it is legally prohibited. What is the strongest response?
practice.answer: Listen respectfully, avoid making a legal determination beyond your role, and help identify the appropriate workplace or external resource.

practice.prompt: A worker is unsure whether a supervisor's conduct violates policy. Is it reasonable to ask an authorized workplace contact for guidance?
practice.answer: Yes. Seeking clarification through an appropriate channel is a responsible step.

quiz.question: What is the strongest response to a serious workplace concern when you are not the decision authority?
options: Use an appropriate reporting or guidance channel
Ignore it because workplace rules are never important
quiz.answer: Use an appropriate reporting or guidance channel

lab.objective: Review simulated workplace situations and identify which appear to be ordinary disagreements, which need clarification, and which should be routed to an appropriate support or reporting channel.

reflectionPrompt: Why is it useful to know how to raise a concern even when you are not responsible for deciding the final outcome?
